packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-18 -- unverified image-only reading (blind first reader)

Exposure: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of this packet. I did nothing beyond the brief's rules.

LAYOUT SURVEY (from image-001.jpg, reduced overview)
- Single paper(?) leaf, portrait, photographed on black with ruler at top and colour checker bottom right. Pencil shelfmark-type note written vertically at lower right margin ("Stams, StA, Frg. 17r"? -- modern archival note, read only as a label).
- Edges ragged; a horizontal fold/crease across the middle (about two thirds down the written block), with a small hole near centre of the crease line. Staining and abrasion, especially lower half.
- Main text: one block of German cursive (current hand, likely 15th/16th c. type script; observation only), long lines, written across the right ~2/3 of the leaf, about 25-26 lines in a first paragraph, then a second short paragraph of about 5 lines beginning lower down with an enlarged/looped initial. First line starts with a large looped initial "V"/"A"-like flourish in left margin.
- Behind / under the cursive, a strong offset or show-through of a narrow multi-column text block in a smaller book hand, rotated 90 degrees (lines run vertically), visible both in the left margin (outside the cursive) and under the cursive itself, appearing reversed. This looks like ink offset or show-through from another text (observation; could also be text on the verso showing through). I do not attempt to read the offset text unless a tile allows.
- Strike-throughs visible in line 1 (end) and line 2 (a word struck through with interlinear replacement above). Some blue marks (small blue strokes) in the left margin near lower third and in line ~2 of second paragraph.
- No running title, no rubrics in red seen at overview scale.

image-002.jpg (native tile, top-left of leaf: left margin + line beginnings of the cursive, lines 1-15 of the main block)
Observation on the background text: at this resolution the vertical underlying text is clearly a small textura/gothic book letter (looks printed or very regular), in narrow columns, and it reads mirror-reversed -- i.e. offset (set-off) or show-through from another sheet, not text written on this face in the normal sense. Not transcribed (reversed, rotated, fragmentary).
Cursive main text, line beginnings only (rest of each line is on the tile(s) to the right). Line numbers count cursive lines from the top of this tile.

SUMMARY OF COVERAGE AND LIMITATIONS
- Read: line beginnings (image-002, -004, -006) and line ends (image-003, -005, -007) of every cursive line of both paragraphs on this face. The tiles cover the full width only by overlap; the centre of some lines (where image-002/-003 and -004/-005 meet) may hold words I have seen only on one side and may have read twice or missed -- seam joins above are provisional.
- Script: German cursive, current hand; "ß" frequent, "vnd" with v, "dz" abbreviation, "/" virgule used once, ":" as line-break mark. Language is Early New High German (observation from word forms: "pawren", "placz", "Nachrichter", "strangulirt", "freytags hernach").
- Best-confidence spans: image-003 l.3-13 and image-005 l.4-13 (line ends), giving e.g. "...vberanndtwurten lassen / ... fengklichen vnthalten worden / ... der Nachrichter, darzue von / ... gebracht werden lassen / mitwa?ß / ... ist vnd freytags hernach vor / ... auf offnem placz fur gericht gestelt, / ... leut Jung vnd alt arm vnd Reich / ... insunderhait ettlich darzu bestelt, / ... gefragt ... sy / ... der lere vnd glaub sy haben ... / ... nit bekennen, sonder auch ... / ... anzaigen sind verstanden, dz sy / ... dieselben schrifft bekennend? strangulirt,".
- Unread/poorly read: line beginnings of lines 7-11 (image-002) and the whole of paragraph 2, both under heavy set-off; the fold lines (main-block l.9-10). The underlying reversed, rotated book-letter text (set-off) was not transcribed; a mirrored, rotated, contrast-enhanced view would be needed to read it.
- [Correction: written before I opened image-008. The packet does contain a second face; see below.]
- Suggested further views: a mirrored+rotated crop of the left margin for the set-off text; a colour-channel separation (the cursive ink is darker/greyer than the brown set-off) for paragraph 2 and lines 7-11.
- I did not hit the image limit.

=== SECOND FACE ===
image-008.jpg (reduced overview of the other face; pencil label lower right "Stams, StA, Frg. 179v"? -- read as label only)
Layout survey: same leaf, same horizontal fold about 60% down. Cursive in the same(?) hand, in three paragraphs: (a) top, ~9 lines beginning with a looped initial in the left margin ("Vnd ..."); (b) middle, ~12 lines starting below a gap, running across the fold; (c) lower, ~11 lines beginning with a large looped initial ("W?..."). Text block again occupies the right ~2/3; left margin carries modern pencil/ink notes rotated vertically ("Orig.? XI/66", "1641-1449"? or a date range, and similar archival marks; not interpreted). Heavy brown water staining and large pale areas where the surface has lost ink (white streaks running vertically in lower half), so many words in paragraphs (b) and (c) are abraded. No set-off book text is visible on this face at overview scale (consistent with the set-off being on the first face only). No rubrics seen.

Pencil archival notes, rotated: "Orig.? IX/66" (or "XI/66") and "?ca. 1641-1649" (the digits are read as seen; not interpreted). Water stain and ink loss over l.6-10.
